questions.q: What is the correct T-SQL syntax to add TotalDue and ShipCity as included columns to a nonclustered index keyed on CustomerId?
options: CREATE INDEX IX_Orders ON dbo.Orders (CustomerId) INCLUDE (TotalDue, ShipCity);
CREATE INDEX IX_Orders ON dbo.Orders (CustomerId, TotalDue, ShipCity);
CREATE INDEX IX_Orders ON dbo.Orders (CustomerId) WHERE (TotalDue, ShipCity);
ALTER INDEX IX_Orders ADD INCLUDE (TotalDue, ShipCity);
questions.explain: The INCLUDE clause adds non-key included columns to a nonclustered index, distinct from the key column list in parentheses.

questions.q: Can an included column be used to seek or sort an index?
options: No — included columns are stored only at the leaf level for retrieval and play no role in the index's sort order
Yes, exactly like a key column
Only if the column is an integer type
Only in a clustered index
questions.explain: Included columns exist purely so a query can read their value without a Key Lookup; they don't participate in the index's sort order or seeking.

questions.q: Why are included columns generally cheaper to add than key columns, per this lesson?
options: Key columns are stored at every level of the index's B-tree, while included columns are stored only at the leaf level
Included columns don't take up any disk space at all
Included columns are automatically compressed while key columns are not
There is no cost difference between the two
questions.explain: Because key columns shape the tree structure, they widen every level of the B-tree; included columns only widen the leaf level.

questions.q: What is one thing an included column can do that a key column cannot, per this lesson?
options: Be a data type like nvarchar(max), varchar(max), or xml that isn't allowed as an index key column at all
Be filtered on with a WHERE clause seek
Determine the index's leftmost-prefix order
Exist without being part of any CREATE INDEX statement
questions.explain: Large object types disallowed as key columns can still be added as included columns, since they only need to be stored for retrieval, not sorted.

questions.q: What is the concrete rule this lesson gives for choosing between a key column and an included column?
options: If a query needs to seek, range-scan, or sort using the column, it must be a key column; if it only needs to be read back once a row is found, it belongs in INCLUDE
Always put every column referenced by any query into the key, in alphabetical order
Included columns should be used only for primary key columns
There is no rule — the choice makes no measurable difference
questions.explain: The lesson frames the decision around whether the column drives seeking/sorting (key) versus is only ever read back after a row is located (INCLUDE).
